ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A barcode as pictured is made up of alternate black and white stripes. The code always starts and ends with a black stripee. Each strip (black or white) has the width 1 or 2 and the total width of the barcode is 12. How many different barcodes if this kind are there if one reads from left to right?

Each stripe (black or white) has width 1 or 2, and the total width of the barcode is 12. How many different barcodes of this kind are there if one reads from left to right?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Count by the total number of stripes k. Since the barcode alternates colors and starts and ends with black, the number of stripes must be odd. Each stripe has width 1 or 2. If t stripes have width 2, then the total width is k + t, because starting with k stripes of width 1 and adding 1 extra unit for each width-2 stripe gives total width k+t. The total width is 12, so t = 12 - k. We need 0 <= t <= k, and k must be odd. Thus k can be 7, 9, or 11. For k=7, t=5, giving C(7,5)=21 choices. For k=9, t=3, giving C(9,3)=84 choices. For k=11, t=1, giving C(11,1)=11 choices. Total: 21 + 84 + 11 = 116.

method.method_draft: Count by the total number of stripes. From the text, the barcode alternates colors, starts black, and ends black, so the number of stripes must be odd. If there are k stripes, each has width 1 or 2 and the total width is 12. Let t be the number of stripes of width 2. Then the total width is k+t=12, so t=12-k. For each feasible odd k, count the choices of which t of the k stripes have width 2. Only k=7,9,11 work, giving C(7,5)+C(9,3)+C(11,1)=21+84+11=116.

method.method_draft: Use a dynamic programming recurrence by total width and ending color. From the text, the first completed stripe must be black and each next stripe has the opposite color and width 1 or 2. Let B(n) be the number of valid partial barcodes of total width n ending with a black stripe, and W(n) the number ending with a white stripe. Initialize B(1)=1 and B(2)=1 for a single black stripe of width 1 or 2, with W(0)=W(1)=0. For n beyond the initial single-stripe cases, append a stripe of width 1 or 2 of the opposite color: B(n)=W(n-1)+W(n-2) plus the single-stripe initialization when n=1,2; W(n)=B(n-1)+B(n-2). Compute these values up to n=12 and take B(12), since the full barcode must end black. This yields 116.
